## Statute
§1(b) - Tax imposed on heads of households
§63(c)(7)(A)(i) - Standard deduction for head of households in 2019
§151(b) - Taxpayer exemption
§151(c) - Dependent exemption
§152(d) - Definition of qualifying relative

## Reasoning
Alice qualifies as Head of Household under §1(b) because:
- Bob (her nephew) lived with her for the entire year 2019
- Alice maintained the household (paid more than half the cost)
- Bob is a qualifying relative under §152(d) because:
  - He is a blood relative (nephew)
  - He had no gross income (below exemption amount)
  - Alice provided more than half his support
  - He cannot be a qualifying child of another taxpayer (Charlie had a different principal place of abode)

Alice's tax calculation:
- Gross income: $34,510
- Standard deduction (Head of Household, §63(c)(7)): $18,000
- Personal exemptions: $4,000 ($2,000 for Alice under §151(b) + $2,000 for Bob under §151(c))
- Taxable income: $34,510 - $18,000 - $4,000 = $12,510

Under §1(b)(i), Head of Household tax is 15% of taxable income up to $29,600:
- Tax = $12,510 × 15% = $1,876.50
- Rounded to whole number: $1,877

- Personal exemptions: $0 (§151(d)(5) sets exemption amount to zero for 2018-2025)
- Taxable income: $34,510 - $18,000 = $16,510

Under §1(b)(i), Head of Household tax is 15% of taxable income up to $29,600:
- Tax = $16,510 × 15% = $2,476.50
